example_input: Summarize the changes in this repo
note: Representations below are simplified shapes of the real types at the pinned SHA, not verbatim dumps.

steps.narrative: The Ink TUI captures the prompt “Summarize the changes in this repo” and submitQuery enters sendMessageStream with SendMessageType.UserQuery. UserPromptSubmit hooks — one of 22 event types on the Claude Code taxonomy — fire once per prompt_id, so skills can expand or veto the prompt before the turn starts. Hooks come in four kinds: command, http (with an SSRF guard), function, and prompt.
steps.representation:
"Summarize the changes in this repo"     # Ink TUI input
  -> submitQuery(prompt)                # use-llm-stream.ts:3555
  -> sendMessageStream(type=UserQuery)  # SendMessageType.UserQuery
  -> UserPromptSubmit hooks             # once per prompt_id
  -> turn begins
steps.title: Input

steps.narrative: boundedTurns = Math.min(turns, 100) caps the recursion at 100 turns, enforced against the max-turns end of the loop. A session turn cap is checked separately, and the session-token-limit gate is evaluated against the model-route identity — so the turn can be refused here, before any model resolution or wire traffic happens.
steps.representation:
turnsRequested
  -> boundedTurns = Math.min(turns, 100)   # client.ts:207
  -> session turn cap check                # client.ts:~4291
  -> session-token-limit gate              # client.ts:4350-4405
     evaluated vs model-route identity
  abort | continue
steps.title: Turn budget

steps.narrative: The loop detector is fed one stream event at a time rather than whole tool results, so repetition is caught incrementally as it streams in. The always-on safeties — 5 identical calls, 8 shell-inspection stagnation events, soft-100/hard-1000 caps — can abort the turn here, before the model is called. When a retry or model-fallback replays the attempt, the detector rolls back its streaks and cap trackers so the replay doesn't trip on its own echo.
steps.representation:
stream event
  -> loopDetectionService.feed(event)   # one event at a time
  -> identical-call streak: 5  -> abort   # loopDetectionService.ts:71
  -> shell-inspection stagnation: 8 -> abort
  -> soft-100 / hard-1000 caps
  always-on check runs before model call  # client.ts:4876-4891
steps.title: Loop guard

steps.narrative: There is no per-turn model router — the composite strategy chain never arrived from the parent, and there is no routing/ directory. resolveForModel picks the content generator for the user's explicitly selected model/provider (via /model or switchModel), resolved fresh at request time. The runtime ModelRegistry is keyed AuthType to a composite id+baseUrl key, with per-model wireApi routing dispatching to one of the six protocol wires.
steps.representation:
selected model/provider   (explicit /model, switchModel)
  -> resolveForModel(model)            # client.ts:4361
  -> ModelRegistry[authType -> id+baseUrl]  # providers/ + models/
  -> ContentGenerator                  # lazy-loaded, per-protocol
  -> wireApi: openai | qwen-oauth | gemini | vertex-ai | anthropic
no routing/ directory
steps.title: Model resolution

steps.narrative: Turn.run drives the model call through LlmChat.sendMessageStream to the resolved wire. MessageDisplay hooks fire as the reply streams in, letting extensions observe or annotate partial output. For our prompt the model emits text plus a single run_shell_command call — git log --oneline -10.
steps.representation:
Turn.run()                         # turn.ts:714
  -> LlmChat.sendMessageStream
  -> MessageDisplay hooks          # client.ts:4737-4765
     fire as the reply streams
  <- wire: text + functionCall
     run_shell_command({command: "git log --oneline -10"})
steps.title: Model call

steps.narrative: Turn yields a ToolCallRequest for the shell command, which the CLI collects and hands to scheduler.schedule(...). The core scheduler walks it through a lifecycle: ValidatingToolCall to ScheduledToolCall to ExecutingToolCall, with the permission gate sitting between validation and execution. Registration of the underlying tools is lazy and mode-gated — factories stay dormant until the mode asks for them.
steps.representation:
ToolCallRequest{run_shell_command, {command: "git log --oneline -10"}}
  -> scheduler.schedule(...)     # use-llm-stream.ts:283
  -> ValidatingToolCall           # coreToolScheduler.ts:605-717
  -> ScheduledToolCall
  -> [permission gate, step 7]
  -> ExecutingToolCall
steps.title: Tool request

steps.narrative: evaluatePermissionFlow runs three layers: L3, the tool's intrinsic getDefaultPermission() — shell is non-read-only so it asks; L4, the PermissionManager evaluating rule strings like "Bash(git *)" with deny > ask > allow > default precedence, session rules before persistent ones. Since AUTO is the default mode, L5 runs the three-layer filter plus a fail-closed LLM classifier over the call — any error blocks. An "Always allow" outcome persists the new rule into settings.json for next time.
steps.representation:
tool call: run_shell_command("git log --oneline -10")
  -> L3: getDefaultPermission() -> ask   # shell, non-read-only
  -> L4: PermissionManager.evaluateSingle  # deny > ask > allow > default
     rules are strings: "Bash(git *)", "Read(./secrets/**)"
  -> L5 (AUTO default): three-layer filter + LLM classifier
     fail-closed: any error -> shouldBlock=true
  -> allow | ask | deny; "Always allow" persists to settings.json
steps.title: Permissions

steps.narrative: The tool executes and its output becomes functionResponse parts. handleCompletedTools calls submitQuery(responses, {isContinuation: true}) with SendMessageType.ToolResult — re-entering the loop at step 2 with boundedTurns - 1, since the loop is recursive sendMessageStream re-entry rather than an iterative processTurn. When no tool calls are pending, the Stop-hook chain runs, then the next-speaker check — skipped by default — and the turn ends.
steps.representation:
tool output
  -> functionResponse parts
  -> handleCompletedTools(responses)    # use-llm-stream.ts:1131
  -> submitQuery(responses, {isContinuation: true})
     type=SendMessageType.ToolResult    # use-llm-stream.ts:3555
  -> back to step 2, boundedTurns - 1
no pending calls -> Stop-hook chain -> next-speaker check (skipped)
